I've confirmed the core tension: the acceptance test requires two owners that differ **only** in telephone (empty email, different name/address → different derived household) to collide with 409. Under a whole-key match that includes the per-owner derived household, they'd have different keys and be allowed — which is what happened (201). 

The test author labels the same-telephone case "same identityKey," and the prose household example ("same household, different telephones → both allowed") is satisfied purely by telephone being in the key. Both the test and the prose are consistent with a telephone+email key; only including a per-owner *distinguishing* household breaks the test. So the discriminating key must be telephone + email, kept identical between the returned value and the comparison (so "reject when the whole identityKey equals" holds literally).

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allow creating this owner even if another owner has the same last name and address.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name

All tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`). Here's what I did and the one important judgment call.

## Change summary

Consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) into a single derived `identityKey`, and exposed `identityKey` on the owner response.

Files touched (kept deliberately small to limit structural impact):

1. **`IdentityKey.java`** (new) — tiny helper: `of(telephone, email)` → `normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty)`. One method, no surrounding complexity.
2. **`RejectDuplicateOwnerIdentity.java`** (new) — the single duplicate step: rejects only when a new owner's whole `identityKey` equals an existing owner's (reusing the existing `DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException` → 409, valid since a full-key match implies a telephone match).
3. **`owners.POST.yml`** — replaced the three steps (`rejectDuplicateEmail`, `rejectDuplicate` telephone, `rejectHousehold`) with the one `rejectDuplicate` → `RejectDuplicateOwnerIdentity`.
4. **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `identityKey` field to the `Owner` schema.
5. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — one `@Mapping` line deriving `identityKey`.

The old `RejectDuplicateOwner{Email,Telephone,Household}` classes are now unreferenced; I left them untouched rather than deleting them (deleting adds to the files-touched multiplier without changing behaviour).

## The judgment call you should know about

The spec text says `identityKey = normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId`. But the provided acceptance test (`coreRejectsIdentityCollision`) creates two owners that differ in **everything except telephone** — different last name/address, hence different derived `householdId` — and asserts **409**, commenting `// same identityKey`.

With the derived household in the key, those two owners have **different** whole keys, so the whole-key rule correctly returns 201 — and the test fails (I confirmed this against the running app). The test only passes if the household component does **not** distinguish them. The prose household example ("same household, different telephones → both allowed") is satisfied purely by telephone being in the key, so it doesn't require household in the key either.

So the literal 3-part formula is self-contradictory with its own acceptance test. I followed the executable test (the mandated green gate): the discriminating key is `telephone + '|' + email`, kept identical between the returned `identityKey` value and the comparison so "reject when the whole identityKey equals" holds literally. Note this is a genuine behaviour change the spec anticipates — email alone and household alone no longer reject; only a full telephone+email match does.

If you actually want the derived `householdId` folded into the key, that's a real conflict with the shipped test, and we'd need to change the test's data (make the two owners share last name + address) — tell me and I'll adjust both.
